entries.title: Moderate-intensity statin in adults 40–75 with diabetes regardless of ASCVD risk
entries.snippet: In adults 40 to 75 years of age with diabetes mellitus, regardless of estimated 10-year ASCVD risk, moderate-intensity statin therapy is indicated.
entries.source_org: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology (Multisociety)
entries.source_doc: 2018 Guideline on the Management of Blood Cholesterol
entries.demo_relevance: Chen (T2DM, LDL 158, exertional chest tightness, FHx premature MI) and Reyes (T2DM age-eligible) both have a class I indication for statin.

entries.title: High-intensity statin in higher-risk diabetes
entries.snippet: In adults 40 to 75 years of age with diabetes mellitus and multiple ASCVD risk factors, it is reasonable to prescribe high-intensity statin therapy with the aim to reduce LDL-C levels by 50% or more.
entries.source_org: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology (Multisociety)
entries.source_doc: 2018 Guideline on the Management of Blood Cholesterol
entries.applies_when: adult 40–75 with DM and ≥1 ASCVD risk-enhancing factor (e.g., FHx premature ASCVD, CKD, long-duration DM, retinopathy/neuropathy/albuminuria, ABI <0.9)
entries.demo_relevance: Chen has T2DM + HTN + dyslipidemia + FHx premature MI + exertional chest pain — multiple risk enhancers warrant high-intensity statin.

entries.title: High-intensity statin (or maximally tolerated) for clinical ASCVD
entries.snippet: In patients who are 75 years of age or younger with clinical ASCVD, high-intensity statin therapy should be initiated or continued with the aim of achieving a 50% or greater reduction in LDL-C levels.
entries.source_org: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology (Multisociety)
entries.source_doc: 2018 Guideline on the Management of Blood Cholesterol
entries.demo_relevance: If Chen's chest tightness workup confirms CAD, immediately escalates to high-intensity secondary-prevention statin.

entries.title: LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL: high-intensity statin without risk assessment
entries.snippet: In patients 20 to 75 years of age with an LDL-C level of 190 mg/dL (≥4.9 mmol/L) or higher, maximally tolerated statin therapy is recommended.
entries.source_org: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology (Multisociety)
entries.source_doc: 2018 Guideline on the Management of Blood Cholesterol
entries.demo_relevance: Boundary check: Chen LDL 158 — does NOT trigger this rule on LDL alone, but does via DM pathway.

entries.title: Intermediate 10-yr ASCVD risk (7.5–<20%) — moderate-intensity statin
entries.snippet: In adults 40 to 75 years of age without diabetes mellitus and with LDL-C levels ≥70 mg/dL, at a 10-year ASCVD risk of ≥7.5%, start a moderate-intensity statin if a discussion of treatment options favors statin therapy. Risk-enhancing factors favor statin therapy.
entries.source_org: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology (Multisociety)
entries.source_doc: 2018 Guideline on the Management of Blood Cholesterol
entries.applies_when: adult 40–75 without DM, LDL 70–189, 10-yr ASCVD risk 7.5–<20%
entries.demo_relevance: Default framework when DM rule does not apply (e.g., Whitaker, Kowalski) — needs ASCVD score.

entries.title: ASCVD risk-enhancing factors (incl. family history of premature ASCVD)
entries.snippet: Risk-enhancing factors include family history of premature ASCVD (men <55 y, women <65 y), persistently elevated LDL-C ≥160 mg/dL, chronic kidney disease, metabolic syndrome, conditions specific to women (e.g., preeclampsia, premature menopause), inflammatory diseases, ethnicity, and persistently elevated triglycerides ≥175 mg/dL.
entries.source_org: American Heart Association / American College of Cardiology (Multisociety)
entries.source_doc: 2018 Guideline on the Management of Blood Cholesterol
entries.applies_when: borderline or intermediate ASCVD risk decision
entries.demo_relevance: Chen: FHx premature MI + TG 178 + LDL 158 → multiple risk enhancers; supports high-intensity statin.
